sph_interpretive_translation: When the appointed representative fails in execution, the appointer shall bear responsibility anew through a designated surety.
executable_legal_axioms: IF representative fails in assigned duty THEN appointer assumes liability via substitute surety
IF capacity to execute is unmet THEN responsibility transfers to source of appointment
IF failure occurs due to misalignment THEN realignment protocol activates with designated replacement
supreme_court_application: In cases where judicially appointed agents or representatives fail in lawful execution, the originating authority must ensure continuity through a qualified substitute surety. The court must verify that the new surety aligns with dharma-based capacity metrics, ensuring no degradation in integrity or function.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This provision reflects pramāṇa-based causality: failure arises from misaligned capacity, not inherent fault. Responsibility flows sequentially from action to agent to appointer. Restoration is achieved by replacing the failed channel without inflicting suffering, preserving cosmic and legal order.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma flows through alignment, not punishment. Responsibility is restored, not enforced. Consciousness remains the ultimate adjudicator.
